entries.title: TRG Music Listings (weekly club calendar), 31 weekly pages naming Doug
entries.notes: Gig calendar entries, NOT reviews. Page URLs are https://chicagoreader.com/news/trg-music-listings-N/ for N in 2, 3, 25, 41-50, 52-59, 63-68, 70, 72-74, 85, 88, 89 (page 51 had no match). Spot-checked: 2003-05-01 lists 'Doug Rosenberg Trio' Fri/Sat at Montage (Naperville), 'Keyon Harrold/Doug Rosenberg Quintet' at Chase Cafe 5/8 and Velvet Lounge 5/7; 2004-06-10 lists 'Goran Ivanovic & Doug Rosenberg' at Chase Cafe 6/11. Useful as dated evidence of regular Chicago gigging 2003-2004; only the other 29 pages are unread beyond the name match. | Bare gig listings, seen only as Google snippets, for the Goran Ivanovic Group at HotHouse (2004-03-12, with Shooglenifty), Hideout/Jazz Showcase (Jazz Institute of Chicago Jazz Club Tour), Around the Coyote Fall Arts Festival, and others across 2004. Useful as a dated record of when the group formed and where it played. Individual URLs are on chicagoreader.com/news/trg-music-listings-NN; not opened. Opened 2026-10-23 via the Reader's current site: trg-music-listings-11/12 (HotHouse 2004-03-12 with Shooglenifty), -20 (Borders Books & Music, 2004-05-09), -23/24 (HotHouse 2004-06-04 with Andreas Kapsalis Trio), -25 (Chase Cafe 2004-06-11, see chireader-trg-chase-cafe-2004-06), -30/31 (Morseland 2004-07-23), -35/36 (Martyrs' 2004-08-28 with New Monsoon), -37 (HotHouse 2004-09-09 with Andreas Kapsalis). All under the name Goran Ivanovic Group, none naming Doug; all before the 2005 start of the show log.

entries.title: JazzPRESS, October 2012: interview with Matt Ulery (Wywiady, pp. 78-80)
entries.author: Interviewer signed "RG" (full name not captured)
pullQuotes: (translated from Polish) "Part of the music was written by Goran Ivanovic, and part is mine."
entries.notes: Not a review: an interview with bassist Matt Ulery in the Polish web magazine's October 2012 issue (113-page PDF). Pages 78 and 80 discuss Eastern Blok: Ulery says the band listened to a lot of Balkan, Russian and Polish folk music when it started, and that Underwater was recorded in a Chicago studio with engineer Anthony Gravino (who made all his records) and is 'my second self'. The interviewer admits he has not yet heard Underwater. Translations are by Claude, not the publisher; check the Polish before quoting. Doug Rosenberg is not named on the pages found.

entries.title: DownBeat, January 2013 (mention)
entries.notes: DownBeat January 2013 issue (a Scribd copy). Snippet reads 'In the quartet Eastern Blok with guitarist Goran Ivanovic, all of the compositions are tied to Balkan traditions.' Probably in a feature on Matt Ulery. Seen only as a Google result titled 'Downbeat-January2013' on Scribd; the link was not captured. This is the first confirmed DownBeat mention; the page and author need finding, and it is a mention, not a review.

entries.title: In the Music Spotlight: Goran Ivanovic Trio
entries.author: Jeff Elbel
entries.notes: Mentions Eastern Blok in passing as a former group (2016, Goran Ivanovic Trio piece). Text seen only as an excerpt on Goran's press page; URL is from a search result and the article was not opened. Date taken from the URL path (2016/3/9). EuroCircle's 2017 profile reprints the piece as 'CHICAGO SUN-TIMES, October 21, 2016, Jeff Elbel', so the dates disagree; confirm on the live page. The text says Goran shared the stage with Michael Caskey 'in the pair's former group Eastern Blok'.

entries.title: Meet Croatian-born guitarist Goran Ivanovic from Chicago
entries.author: Kaisa Kokkonen
entries.notes: Profile of Goran written years after the band ended. Names Eastern Blok as 'a key member of the quartet' with Matt Ulery, Doug Rosenberg and Michael Caskey, a combo that 'deftly surveys the folk music of Macedonia, Bulgaria, and Serbia'. The same text appears on the All About Jazz musician page, so it is probably Goran's own bio. Reprints a Jeff Elbel Sun-Times piece as 'October 21, 2016' (see suntimes-goran-trio-2016-03). The first URL in the leads list (.../meet-croatian-born-guitarist-goran-ivanovic-from-chicago/) was a 404.

entries.title: Customer reviews, Goran Ivanovic Group (Balkan Song Records)
entries.author: Ellen M. Falbowski; Emily Covington; "Somebody of no consequence"
pullQuotes: the horn really is key here
a captivating fusion of traditional Balkan music and acoustic jazz
entries.notes: Three 5-star reviews: 2007-07-05 (Ellen M. Falbowski, who heard the band "in Connecticut in September 2006", a date not in the show log, which has Bradford CT on 2006-03-28), 2013-05-09 (Emily Covington) and 2020-03-10 (a longer one that names "Douglas Rosenberg's saxophone" and argues the horn is what makes the album work). Same page quotes a CD Baby review by Tamara Turner and the All About Jazz line. Read in Chrome 2026-10-23; the page was not saved to press-archive because it was logged in and showed the reader's delivery address. | CD Baby staff review, reproduced in the Amazon listing's editorial reviews; not seen on CD Baby itself, no date.

entries.title: Goran Ivanovic Group (AllMusic review by Chris Nickson)
entries.author: Chris Nickson
pullQuotes: a killer jazz disc
has far more in common with jazz than its roots
entries.notes: Staff review read in Chrome. Mixed-to-positive: praises Ivanovic's inventive guitar and the writing, but warns that listeners wanting gypsy music will not get it. No publication date on the page. The star rating is graphical and was not captured; check the page. Page lists the album as 2005, recorded July 2005 at B-Side Audio. The AllMusic page for Folk Tales shows no review. Does not name Doug in the text read.

entries.title: Chicago Tribune quote used in bio and label copy
entries.author: Howard Reich
pullQuotes: fearlessness of spirit and a robustness of tone that seem likely to win him a devoted following in coming years
